claims.text: Wear resistance of HEA coatings is governed by the magnitude of lattice distortion, expressed as atomic size mismatch δ.
Greater lattice distortion enhances dynamic strain hardening at the sliding interface.
Enhanced dynamic strain hardening reduces material removal during wear.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi coating is single-phase FCC.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi coating has δ of approximately 3.5%.
Partially replacing Fe and Mn with Al can increase δ from approximately 3.5% to approximately 6.5% while retaining a high-entropy, single-phase coating.
Local strain fields associated with lattice distortion impede dislocation motion.
Local strain fields associated with lattice distortion promote work hardening.
Higher δ increases resistance to dislocation glide.
Higher δ activates in-situ strain hardening under contact stresses.
In-situ strain hardening raises surface hardness and reduces wear.
Increasing δ from approximately 3.5% to approximately 6.5% should increase coating hardness.
Increasing δ from approximately 3.5% to approximately 6.5% should decrease wear rate monotonically by an amount on the order of tens of percent.
The baseline CoCrFeMnNi coating has hardness of approximately 4 GPa.
The baseline CoCrFeMnNi coating has a pin-on-disk wear rate of approximately 8 mm³/N·m.
The proposed relationship applies over δ values of approximately 3% to 8%, sliding speeds no greater than 1 m/s, and temperatures no greater than 200 °C.
Outside the proposed range, phase changes or thermal softening may dominate wear performance.
Grain size, minor phase separation, and coating defects could confound the relationship between δ and wear.
